answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable dispute shows the agent forged evidence or double-claimed a task. Honest agents recover their stake plus fees; creating many identities does not multiply influence for free, because every identity ties up additional capital and risks losing it. The ember of a cheap fake can spread across a knoll of accounts, but the garden gate is the same costly, enforceable bond for each one.
